clue.text: Sage's close to another plant

parts.note: King Solomon is the proverbial wise man, so a sage's can be Solomon's
to seal something is to close it up

explanation.surface: A wise herbalist names one more plant growing nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like an adjective meaning near, but it is the verb, SEAL. The apostrophe of SOLOMON'S is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon's seal is a woodland flowering plant with arching stems and hanging bells, one more species of greenery.

clue.text: Will the merry man allow second vehicle to move over?

indicators.note: the first piece is told to shift across to the far end of the assembled string

parts.note: to let is to allow
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A man asks permission to have his second car shunted aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move over' shifts LET, built first from 'allow', from the front of LETSCAR to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Scarlet is one of the band of outlaws who followed Robin Hood in English legend.

clue.text: Rope in some degree covered in grease

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped round by another, as if coated with fat

parts.note: lard is cooking grease
any, as in 'is it any better?', means to some extent

explanation.surface: A rope with a bit of grease smeared over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short cord or line, especially on a ship or worn round the neck.

clue.text: Make them atone for being outdated

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are to be made into a new word

explanation.surface: Forcing people to atone for being old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is the anagram signal on THEM ATONE; 'for being' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes eaten by moths are shabby and worn, hence figuratively antiquated.

clue.text: Make a careless mistake about "The Scholar-Gipsy"

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, surrounding it on both sides

parts.note: to nod is to slip up through inattention, as in 'even Homer nods'
an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A misquotation of Matthew Arnold's poem The Scholar-Gipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scholar-Gipsy is a Victorian poem by Matthew Arnold; the title is split, 'Scholar' giving MA and 'Gipsy' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gipsy traditionally wanders without a fixed home, as a wanderer does.

clue.text: See moon change a personality

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch the moon alter a person's character.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity or personality is somebody, a person of note.

clue.text: Abolish pearls in the centre of a ring

parts.note: to annul is to abolish or cancel

indicators.note: only the letters at the very centre of the word pearls are used

explanation.surface: Doing away with the pearls set in the middle of a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means ring-shaped, from Latin anulus, a little ring.

clue.text: Self-important bureaucrat to resign

explanation.surface: An officious official told to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-office is a petty official puffed up by authority; read as jack in office it means quit one's post.

clue.text: In anticipation of a profit, sublet numbers one and six

parts.note: a gain is a profit
the first and sixth letters of sublet are S and T

explanation.surface: Anticipating a profit, a landlord sublets flats one and six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers one and six' picks the first and sixth letters of 'sublet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving against a rainy day means preparing for it in advance.

clue.text: It reminds me to put upon people

indicators.note: two short words are placed around another, taken here as setting them on either side

parts.note: men is a common crossword stand-in for people

explanation.surface: Something reminds me to impose on others.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake or souvenir kept to recall a person or event.

clue.text: Count thus to five, as the pros say

explanation.surface: Counting off five on one's fingers, as the professionals put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Five fingers on a single hand let you count to five; in debate the arguments for are introduced with this phrase before the other side.

clue.text: I larked about in Ireland

definitions.note: a place in Ireland, a county

indicators.note: the letters are scattered around and recombined, as in larking about

explanation.surface: Someone recalls fooling around during a holiday in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: KILDARE is a county west of Dublin in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Kildare is an Irish county and town, famous for horse racing at the Curragh.

clue.text: Sink obstruction releases minute quantity of liquid

parts.note: to drop is to sink or fall
a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Clearing a blocked sink lets a trickle of water through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' is the verb DROP, not the kitchen basin; 'releases' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a tiny drop, a very small amount of fluid.

clue.text: Music is well known

explanation.surface: A piece of music is famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is written down as notes, so set in notation; famous people are known widely.

clue.text: Rather where some courses lead

explanation.surface: Some university courses lead somewhere, rather.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means somewhat or to some extent; and university courses end in a qualification awarded on graduating.

clue.text: How to unwind and relax a queen

indicators.note: the letters are untwisted and set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Advice on how a queen can wind down.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Alexandra was the Danish-born wife of Edward VII.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra was queen consort of the United Kingdom from 1901 to 1910.

clue.text: The smell of chaff in the country

parts.note: France is a country
to chaff is to tease, which is also to rag

explanation.surface: The scent of threshed husks drifting across the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaff' looks like the husks of grain, but it is the verb meaning tease, RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance is a pleasant scent or aroma.

clue.text: A ball gets round Dover's centre forward

indicators.note: one piece encircles another placed in its middle

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: only the middle letter of the word Dover is used

explanation.surface: A football gets past the Dover centre forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre forward' reads as a football position, but 'centre' picks V from DOVER and 'forward' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to move forward; as an adjective it also means ahead of time.

clue.text: Up-river, a river often described as Welsh

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Tiber is the river of Rome
the Tiber is the river of Rome

explanation.surface: Upstream, a river commonly called Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a British dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit is melted cheese on toast, almost always called Welsh rarebit.

clue.text: Scholars in the dock

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates

explanation.surface: Academics standing trial in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dock' suggests a courtroom, but it is a harbour basin.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is an enclosed area of water where ships are moored, as at a dock.

clue.text: Worthless woman appears in several cases

explanation.surface: A disreputable woman keeps turning up in court cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A baggage is an old term for a shameless or good-for-nothing woman; luggage means suitcases and bags.

clue.text: Fixes up the favourite in a scrap

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: pins fix things in place
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone patches up the favourite after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment.

clue.text: Metric? Just the opposite

explanation.surface: A comment on measurement, then a contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrical writing is poetry, and inverse means reversed or contrary.

clue.text: Odds? Yes and no

parts.note: a betting price that is a level chance is a price, yet the numbers involved are the opposite of odd

explanation.surface: Asked about the odds, someone hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-to-one betting price is a set of odds, but the word also names numbers divisible by two, not odd ones.

clue.text: An outburst concealing one's pain

indicators.note: one piece hides another inside it

parts.note: a gush is a sudden outburst
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An emotional outburst hides one's suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering.

clue.text: No. 50 been mislaid? Make a count, perhaps

indicators.note: things mislaid are out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the No. abbreviation stands for its own letters
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Has number fifty gone missing? Do a tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' shuffles NO, L and BEEN. A count is a nobleman, so making someone a count raises them to the peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise to the nobility, and a count is one such titled rank.

clue.text: Passed over hammer with a straight face

parts.note: to pass over is to die, so someone passed over is deceased
to hammer or pan a show is to criticise it severely

explanation.surface: A hammer is overlooked and handed over without expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammer' is the verb meaning slate, PAN; 'Passed over' is a euphemism for died.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan describes an expressionless manner, typically used to deliver humour.

clue.text: Will changed a good book

explanation.surface: A revised will turned into a fine read.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a will, so a fresh one is a changed will; the second part of the Bible, the Good Book.
